html:
The Mongolian democratic revolution of 1990 was a peaceful movement that ended about seventy years of one party communist rule in Mongolia.

It was inspired by Gorbachev's reforms in the Soviet Union and the revolutions of 1989 in Eastern Europe. From December 1989 young people, led by a new Mongolian Democratic Union and figures such as Sanjaasürengiin Zorig, held rallies on Sükhbaatar Square in Ulaanbaatar, named after the hero of the 1921 revolution. In March 1990 a hunger strike on the square brought the resignation of the ruling party's leaders.

The first multi-party elections followed in July 1990. The former ruling party won them, but it accepted reform. A new constitution in 1992 made Mongolia a parliamentary democracy with a free market. Unlike in China a year earlier, at Tiananmen Square, no one was shot.
sum: The Mongolian democratic revolution of 1990 was a peaceful movement that ended about seventy years of one party communist rule in Mongolia.
